answer: The Original Costa Route is a 7-day Costa Rica itinerary from James Wild & Co. built only on Cayuga Collection hotels: three nights at Senda Monteverde in the cloud forest and three at Kura, the adults-only hotel above Uvita, with a stop at Dominical, where James has surfed since the early 1990s. You travel by private driver from San José.

days.title: San José to the cloud forest
days.line: Private driver up to Monteverde · ~3.5 hr
days.body: Met at San José airport and driven up into the mountains. The last stretch climbs into cool air and cloud; you arrive at Senda Monteverde for the first evening above the forest.
days.acts: Arrival · first evening in the cloud forest
days.imgAlt: A balcony looking over the cloud forest at Senda Monteverde

days.title: The Aguti trails
days.line: Walk as far as your legs go
days.body: Senda guests walk the neighbouring Aguti Wildlife Reserve as often as they like. Go early with a naturalist, come back for lunch, and take the night walk after dark when the frogs come out.
days.imgAlt: Birders looking up at a giant buttressed tree at Senda Monteverde

days.title: Quetzal at dawn
days.line: A birding guide and a telescope
days.body: Out at first light for the quetzal, then a free afternoon. The hot pools are in the forest; nobody has ever regretted using them.
days.imgAlt: A resplendent quetzal in flight among cloud-forest trees at Senda Monteverde

days.title: Down to Uvita, by way of Dominical
days.line: Private driver to the south Pacific · ~5 hr
days.body: The long drive of the trip, down from the mountains and south along the coast. Lunch at Dominical, where James sat for his 1995 photo, then on to Kura above Uvita.
days.imgAlt: Kura's infinity pool deck looking over the Pacific at Uvita

days.title: The Whale's Tail
days.body: At low tide the sandbar at Marino Ballena National Park makes the shape of a whale's tail, and you can walk it. In season, a boat goes out for the humpbacks [season and tides to confirm].
days.move: Short drive · on foot · boat in season
days.acts: Whale's Tail walk · whale watching in season
days.imgAlt: A humpback whale breaching beside a whale-watching boat

days.title: The founder's surf day
days.body: A board sized for you is waiting. If Dominical is working, you surf Dominical; if not, a local guide takes you to a secret spot James keeps off the page. Or nothing at all: Kura is adults only and built for doing very little.
days.imgAlt: Polaroid of James relaxing on a beach in a patterned shirt, Dominical, Costa Rica, 1995

days.title: Home
days.body: The drive back to San José, about 3.5 hours, or a short domestic flight from the south Pacific [confirm], and the flight home. If the swell is running at Pavones, James will tell you before you leave: cancel the flight and head south.
days.imgAlt: Footprints in the sand on a beach looking out to small islands at Arenas del Mar

founder.title: Surf travel since 1992. Cayuga since 1994.
founder.p1: James has pioneered surf travel in Costa Rica since 1992, when the boards rode on the roof and the coast road was mostly a rumour. He has followed Hans Pfister, Cayuga's co-founder, since 1994, from his early days selling these lodges.
founder.p2: This is the week he'd hand a couple: the cloud forest first, then the quiet south Pacific above Uvita, a board waiting at the coast, and lunch at Dominical, where his 1995 photo was taken.

faqs: Is 7 days enough for Costa Rica?
Seven days covers two places well: the Monteverde cloud forest and the south Pacific at Uvita. Adding a third usually means more road than holiday. With ten days, take the 10-day version.
How far is Monteverde from Uvita?
About five hours by private driver, with lunch at Dominical on the way. It's the only long drive on the route.
Which Cayuga hotels does this route use?
Senda Monteverde in the cloud forest and Kura above Uvita, both part of the Cayuga Collection.
Is this route good for families?
Kura is adults only, so this week suits couples. Families should take the 10-day version, which uses Arenas del Mar.
Can I surf on this trip?

Yes. A board sized for you waits at the coast and you surf Dominical if it's happening, or a local guide takes you to a secret spot James keeps off the page. Beginners are welcome; the guide picks the spot for the swell.

Pavones, near the Panama border, is one of the longest left-hand waves anywhere, and it only really works on the right swell. If it's running when you're due to leave, James will let you know. Cancel your flight, head south, and we'll rebook you home.
Are there offers on this route?
Often. In 2026 Senda Monteverde has stay 3 nights, pay 2, and Kura has stay 4 nights, pay 3 if you add a night. We apply whatever fits your dates.
